aliases: channel capacity: a binary symmetric link
purpose: How much information can one use of the noisy link carry?
meaning: Channel capacity C is the largest mutual information per channel use among the allowed input distributions. For a memoryless binary symmetric channel with flip probability p, C=1−H₂(p) bits per use. A chosen probability q of sending one gives received-one chance t=p+q(1−2p) and mutual information I=H₂(t)−H₂(p). An equally likely input mix reaches the capacity; an uneven mix can supply less information through the same link.

definition.setting: A remote workshop sends a binary machine-status symbol: zero or one. Each use independently flips either symbol with probability p. A designer also chooses the long-run probability q of sending one. Change the channel or the chosen input mix, then compare the information delivered by that mix with the channel’s best possible information per use.

definition.domain_notes: Capacity is an asymptotic coding limit in bits per channel use. It is not a promise that an individual symbol arrives correctly, a rate in bits per second, or a code constructed by this lesson. An always-flipping link is invertible when its rule is known. Printed readings approximate the analytic quantities.

For a memoryless binary symmetric channel with flip probability p, C=1−H₂(p) bits per use. properties.derivation: For this channel, the conditional output entropy is H₂(p), independent of the input symbol. The received-one probability follows by adding the two disjoint input/output routes. Thus I=H₂(t)−H₂(p). Binary output entropy is at most one bit. Choosing q=1/2 makes t=1/2, attains that bound and gives C=1−H₂(p).

steps.reason: For this channel, the conditional output entropy is H₂(p), independent of the input symbol. The received-one probability follows by adding the two disjoint input/output routes.
